properties.name: mqtt.session-expiry
properties.description: How long the broker keeps this client's session, and everything queued for it, after a disconnect. Defaults to the MQTT 5 maximum (a 32-bit second count), i.e. never. This is not message expiry: anything queued while the client is away should generally outlive the outage.

properties.name: mqtt.username
properties.description: Broker username. Leave unset for an anonymous broker.

properties.name: mqtt.password
properties.description: Broker password. Supply from a secret store, never a checked-in properties file.

properties.name: mqtt.dead-letter.topic
properties.description: Topic that unhandleable messages are published to. Required when dead-lettering is enabled. A single topic: the original topic travels inside the envelope, so one ACL grant covers it.

values.description: At most once. Loses messages on an unreliable link.
At least once. The default; expect duplicates and handle them idempotently.
Exactly once. Two extra round trips per message.
In-memory: in-flight QoS 1 messages are lost on restart.
The connection acknowledges after the listener returns without throwing. A failing listener is not acknowledged, so the broker redelivers on session resume.
The listener owns acknowledgement via an MqttAcknowledgement parameter. Use when 'handled' means durable somewhere else.
No retry (default). A failing handler dead-letters immediately.
Retry twice inline before dead-lettering. Retries block the dispatch thread, so keep this small.
